core_obligations: Apply the codimension one quasi-finiteness criterion to get quasi-finiteness of f at every point of the fibre over y (proof lines 3289-3290).
Conclude that the fibre is discrete by the pointwise characterization of quasi-finiteness, and hence finite because it is quasi-compact as a fibre of a proper morphism (proof lines 3290-3293).
Apply the finiteness neighbourhood lemma to conclude that f is finite over some open neighbourhood of y (proof lines 3294-3296).
difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f: X to Y and a point y whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one, under any of the listed hypotheses at generic points of X, the lemma produces an open neighbourhood V of y over which f is finite (statement lines 3267-3286). The proof chains three observations: the quasi-finiteness criterion for the codimension one case makes f quasi-finite at every point of the fibre over y; quasi-finiteness at a point makes the fibre discrete, hence quasi-compact as f is proper, hence finite; and the standard result that a proper morphism with finite fibre over a point is finite over some neighbourhood of that point finishes (proof lines 3288-3296). The claim is H2: three cited inputs in a fixed order, with the finiteness of the fibre as the step that converts discreteness into something the neighbourhood lemma can use.
